# MessageEvent

[Event index](../events.md) · [Dispatcher behavior](../../guides/events.md)

## Fields

| Field | Python type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `Any` | Native Message or MessageService associated with the event. Payload repr is redacted; reading text/media is still sensitive application data. |
| `edited` | `bool` | False for new-message events; True for edits. It reflects event routing, not whether every field has changed. |
| `client` | `Client \| None` | Bound Client used by event reply/edit/delete/download/answer helpers. Detached events can have None; helpers then raise LifecycleError. |
| `chat_type` | `Optional[Literal['private', 'group', 'channel']]` | private, group or channel when the message peer can be classified; None when unavailable. Basic groups and supergroups are not collapsed into an invented wire type. |

## Read-only properties

### chat_id

Marked chat identity when known. Non-channel deletion and inline callback events may have None; never guess the peer from a global message ID.

### outgoing

True when the bound message has its native out flag set. A false value is not a guarantee that a sender entity is available.

### sender_id

Account ID associated with the author/query/status update when available. This is not automatically a complete User object.

### text

Literal message text (or empty string for a service message). It may include private content and is not safe logging data by default.

## delete

Delete the bound message through scoped Client.delete_messages. Returns the batch result list. Channel deletion requires explicit revoke=True, just as on Client.

```python
async def delete(*, revoke: bool = False) -> Any
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Python type | Default | Passing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `revoke` | `bool` | `False` | Keyword-only |

### revoke

Explicit request to remove messages for other participants where supported. Non-channel deletion validates all IDs against the target first. Channels always delete for everyone and therefore require revoke=True.

## download

Download supported document/photo media from the bound message to the explicit destination. Returns the underlying Path/None contract. No automatic filename derived from untrusted media is selected.

```python
async def download(destination: str) -> Any
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Python type | Default | Passing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `destination` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |

### destination

New filesystem path or writable binary stream. Path targets never overwrite existing files and use a temporary sibling plus atomic finalization. Caller streams stay open and may retain partial bytes if the transfer fails.

## edit

Edit the bound message through Client.edit_message. Returns native Updates, not a refreshed Message. Account ownership/permissions apply; no formatting parser is added.

```python
async def edit(text: str) -> Any
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Python type | Default | Passing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |

### text

Literal text for this operation. No implicit Markdown or HTML parser is applied. Pass explicit native entities where the signature supports them; unsupported parse_mode/formatting keywords are not accepted.

## reply

Send literal text in reply to the bound message. Returns a native Message. The original message ID and peer are supplied by the event, while only the documented text/silent arguments can be changed.

```python
async def reply(text: str, *, silent: bool = False) -> Message
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Python type | Default | Passing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |
| `silent` | `bool` | `False` | Keyword-only |

### text

Literal text for this operation. No implicit Markdown or HTML parser is applied. Pass explicit native entities where the signature supports them; unsupported parse_mode/formatting keywords are not accepted.

### silent

When True, requests silent delivery or a silent pin notification. It does not make content invisible, bypass permissions or guarantee that no recipient UI changes occur.

## Example

```python
from gramflux import buttons, filters
from gramflux.raw import types

@client.on_message(filters.incoming & filters.text)
async def handler(event):
    await event.reply("Received")
```

Register before connecting. Callbacks are awaited sequentially, errors are reported through the dispatcher, and shutdown cancellation does not commit an update merely because it was enqueued. Helpers require a bound client/context and raise LifecycleError for detached events; RPC/deadline/cancellation errors propagate normally.

Raw field availability is not uniform across constructor variants. There is no exactly-once durable callback journal, and replays/duplicates across process failures remain possible. See the dispatcher and update-state guides for the complete commitment boundary.
